> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> SEC EDGAR's structured-data products (Form 13F under clean_full/edgar_13f, insider Forms 3/4/5 under clean_full/edgar_insider) are published as a DIRECTORY of per-period bulk zips (one quarterly/rolling-window zip per dataset key, each fanning out to many per-table relational parquets). There is NO server-side row-level date filter (so S2 extend_by_date is out), and it is not one monolithic bulk file (so S5 bulk_snapshot is out) — it is the giant change-feed shape: scrape the data-sets PAGE (the catalogue), diff published dataset keys vs the on-disk partition inventory, and fetch ONLY the NEW keys. Per-period partitioning makes a new quarter a pure addition; existing partitions are never rewritten. The fetcher (updater/strategies/fetchers/sec_edgar.py) implements the S4 current_vintage()+update() contract directly because the payload is RELATIONAL tables (composite/surrogate keys, no series_key/obs_date), not the long-format the generic _giant.run_giant driver assumes.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: Scrape the two data-sets PAGES (form-13f-data-sets, insider-transactions-data-sets) for every published <key>_form13f.zip / <key>_form345.zip. current_vintage() hashes the full published-keys list across both products into one token; a NEW key (new quarter / new rolling window) moves the token. detect_change short-circuits a no-op tick when the token is unmoved. (No per-key Last-Modified probe yet: a SILENT re-publish of an already-on-disk key is not auto-detected; that is acceptable because merge.merge_and_write would dedup+revise it anyway when forced.)
- `since_param`: n/a (no server-side row-level date param on the bulk-zip path; the on-disk partition inventory IS the watermark — update() fetches exactly the published keys absent from disk, plus any key whose last run was partial/failed).
- `out_paths_note`: Multi-product, multi-dir. edgar_13f: data/clean_full/edgar_13f/<TABLE>/period=<key>/<TABLE>.parquet (7 tables; INFOTABLE is the ~118M-row holdings table). edgar_insider: data/clean_full/edgar_insider/<table>/year=<YYYY>/<table>_<key>.parquet (8 tables). Per-product change-feed state sidecar: data/clean_full/_sec_edgar_incr_state.json. Raw zip caches at data/raw/sec_edgar/form13f/ and _raw_insider_zips/. The XBRL companyfacts product (clean_grouped/sec_edgar) and edgar_pointers are NOT owned here.
- `rate_note`: No API key. SEC REQUIRES a descriptive User-Agent or returns 403 (set to 'Econ-Fin Data Library admin@hfdatalibrary.com'). SEC fair-access ~10 req/s; the fetcher sleeps 0.5s between key downloads, 4-attempt backoff, 600s zip timeout. A 404/429/5xx/timeout/bad-zip is TRANSIENT (key stays not-done, source result partial, re-runs next tick). MAX_KEYS_PER_TICK=8 caps a wiped-inventory runaway -> partial.

  REGISTRY (here)  -> the relational Form 13F + insider products under

                      (122,053,194 and 37,169,724 rows of wide tables; no

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S4 fetcher — SEC EDGAR structured-data sets (giant_changed_units).

WHAT THIS COVERS
================
SEC EDGAR publishes several *relational* structured-data products as quarterly
(or rolling-window) bulk ZIPs on its data-sets pages. Two of them are already
materialized on disk as multi-table parquet libraries this fetcher OWNS and keeps
fresh incrementally:

  edgar_13f      Form 13F institutional-holdings data sets
                 clean_full/edgar_13f/<TABLE>/period=<datasetKey>/<TABLE>.parquet
                 7 tables: SUBMISSION, COVERPAGE, OTHERMANAGER, OTHERMANAGER2,
                 INFOTABLE (holdings), SIGNATURE, SUMMARYPAGE  (join: ACCESSION_NUMBER)

  edgar_insider  Forms 3/4/5 insider-transaction data sets
                 clean_full/edgar_insider/<table>/year=<YYYY>/<table>_<YYYYqQ>.parquet
                 8 tables: submission, reportingowner, nonderiv_trans,
                 nonderiv_holding, deriv_trans, deriv_holding, footnotes,
                 owner_signature  (join: ACCESSION_NUMBER)

A third product, edgar_pointers (clean_full/edgar_pointers/cik_shard=NNN/part.parquet:
cik,ticker,form,filing_date,accession,primary_doc_url), is NOT a bulk-zip change
feed — it is built by a per-CIK crawl of data.sec.gov submissions and has no
single catalogue page to diff. It is intentionally OUT of scope here and noted in
the report (it needs its own daily-index delta fetcher, not this one). This module
NEVER touches edgar_pointers.

WHY giant_changed_units (S4), not extend_by_date / bulk_snapshot
================================================================
The natural incremental unit is a *new published dataset key* (a new quarter or
rolling 3-month window), NOT a row-level date tail: the SEC bulk-zip endpoints
expose NO server-side date filter, so a per-row delta (S2) is impossible. But it
is also NOT one monolithic bulk file (S5) — it is a *directory of per-period
artifacts* (one zip per quarter, fanning out to many per-table parquet files),
exactly the giant change-feed shape: download the data-sets PAGE (the catalogue),
diff the published keys against what is already on disk, and fetch ONLY the keys
that are NEW (or whose last run was partial/failed). Per-period partitioning makes
a new quarter a pure ADDITION — old partitions are never rewritten. This is the
S4 contract; the engine lives here per fetchers/_giant.py's design note, because
EDGAR's payload is relational tables (no series_key/obs_date), not the long-format
(series_key,obs_date,value) the generic _giant.run_giant driver assumes.

DUPLICATION GUARD — KEY FORMAT MATCHES EXISTING ON-DISK FORMAT
=============================================================
The on-disk EDGAR parquet has NO `series_key`/`obs_date` columns; row identity is
RELATIONAL. We therefore do NOT invent a series_key (that would not match the
existing format and would not merge). Instead each table is merged into its own
per-period file with the EXACT existing columns and a TABLE-SPECIFIC dedup key —
the SEC surrogate key (`*_SK`) plus ACCESSION_NUMBER where one exists, else the
filing's natural composite. Because new quarters land in their own partition file,
re-running is idempotent (dedup is a no-op) and a re-published quarter REVISES in
place (new rows win) and never-shrinks (merge.merge_and_write guards it). The
dataset key is carried in the partition PATH and in the provenance columns
(DATASET_PERIOD/period for 13f), never minted into a row key — so it cannot
duplicate the file on republish.

HONEST STATUS (the dominant correctness rule)
=============================================
Each (product, dataset-key) pair is one sub-unit. A 429 / 5xx / timeout / network
drop / truncated-or-bad ZIP -> TransientError -> the key stays unselected-as-done
(its vintage is NOT advanced) and the SOURCE result is `partial`; the orchestrator
does NOT stamp last_success and the key re-runs next tick. A 200 page that yields
ZERO catalogue keys is a structural break (TransientError -> retry, never laundered
into no_change). Empty individual tables inside a real quarter are legitimate (SEC
emits empty OTHERMANAGER2 etc.) and are written as 0-row partitions, not failures.
Existing data is only ever EXTENDED via merge.merge_and_write (atomic, dedup,
never-shrink), so a bad fetch can never shrink or duplicate good data.
```

</details>

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='sec_edgar'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source sec_edgar --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source sec_edgar --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('sec_edgar');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source sec_edgar
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Four separate fixes, in priority order. (1) DEDUPE THE STORED PARQUETS (ember + idb, and sweep the class): the first-pass ingesters wrote rows whose (series_key, obs_date) is not unique -- idb's rows_to_long emits ~99% duplicate keys on the social-indicators resources -- so every subsequent merge collapses the file and merge.py:323 refuses. Run a one-off store-side dedup rewrite of the affected parquets (idb: the 11 social-indicators files; ember: the 4 named datasets), and add a test that a fetcher's own key builder produces unique dedup keys, or the same files re-fail on the next first-pass. Note turkiye unlicensed_capacity_chart is a GENUINE upstream shrink 1058->498 and needs an explicit lower min_ratio or a deliberate overwrite, not dedup. (2) GIVE IDB A ROTATION BOOKMARK (load_rotation/rotate_after from _common, exactly as worldbank_esg got in R190) -- without it 1,875 of 1,918 resources are unreachable forever -- and fix the skip predicate so an examined-but-empty resource (sidecar advanced, no parquet written) does not re-enter `todo` every run. (3) WORLDBANK_ESG: stop treating the API's `[{"message":[{"id":"120","key":"Invalid value"}]}]` envelope as an empty window (worldbank_esg.py:95) -- detect the message envelope and file it as a structural/recode signal; then enumerate from /v2/source/75/indicator instead of from the store (worldbank_esg.py:115) and map the 13 dead ids to their new ones (CC.EST->GOV_WGI_CC.EST etc., EN.ATM.*->EN.GHG.*.AR5) as an in-place repair preserving live series ids, per the imf_hpdd/imf_fiscaldecentralization precedent in config.py. The 8/9 itself needs no fix -- WB 502'd for 20 minutes and is fine now -- though capping get_json's ladder (6 tries x 120 s + ~61 s backoff burns the whole 20-min budget on ~9 indicators) and wiring the existing TransientStreak would stop a WB outage from costing a whole tick. (4) HOUSEKEEPING: delete the fred_releases row from state.db (and consider deleting the orphaned fetcher) so a de-registered source stops appearing in failure triage; re-run sec_edgar to prove commit 3d7f4e3e actually clears edgar_insider/2026q2 -- it has not been attempted since the fix landed. ksh_stadat needs nothing.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
